findings.highlight: it’s a burden on you, right?
findings.evidenceJa: 実際セイバーは多くの制約を負ってるんだろう
findings.governingReading: Shirou insists that Saber is in fact operating under many restrictions.
findings.explanation: The English replaces concrete plural constraints on her power with a generic emotional or practical burden.

findings.highlight: it may be impossible for any Servant to beat that giant
findings.evidenceJa: あの巨人を追い詰める事は不可能かもしれない
findings.governingReading: Saber says it may be impossible for any Servant even to drive the giant into a corner.
findings.explanation: “Beat” skips from inability to pressure Berserker to inability to defeat him, weakening the escalation of Saber’s assessment.

findings.evidenceJa: バーサーカーを守る“[ruby text=ことわり]理”
findings.governingReading: The “principle” or governing law protecting Berserker lies outside physical law.
findings.explanation: mirror moon mistakes the displayed kanji 理 for “refusal” and ignores its ことわり reading, destroying the metaphysical explanation.

findings.highlight: So we need to stay away from
findings.evidenceJa: 結局、撤退が大前提なんだな
findings.governingReading: Shirou recognizes that retreat remains the fundamental premise of their response.
findings.explanation: The English turns a tactical requirement to retreat into temporary general avoidance and introduces a plural target.

findings.highlight: And the anti-castle Noble Phantasms decides everything in a single blow.
findings.evidenceJa: そして一撃で全てを決する対城宝具
findings.governingReading: Anti-fortress Noble Phantasms settle everything in one blow.
findings.explanation: The plural subject takes a singular verb in a core classification statement.

findings.evidenceJa: バーサーカーが彼女の守護に徹するのなら
findings.governingReading: If Berserker devotes himself entirely to protecting Illyasviel, Saber will be unable to protect Shirou completely.
findings.explanation: The English reverses protector and protected, changing the enemy pair’s proposed strategy and Saber’s reason for fearing it.
